title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
author: Jan Maarten
description: GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.md files and helps maintainers document accessibility goals, known barriers, supported environments, contributor expectations, and reporting processes. The post Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
summary: Accessibility work often lives in issue trackers, contribution guidelines, audit reports, team knowledge, and conversations with users. When that information has no predictable home, people who encounter a barrier must search for it, and maintainers lose context as contributors and project ownership change.
takeaways: Accessibility statements make project practices visible GitHub CLI’s accessibility statement , for example, documents settings, known barriers, and workarounds.

The GitHub Annotation Toolkit’s accessibility statement documents a limitation of its Figma library: annotations use canvas position, connecting lines, and matching numbers to visually convey relationships.
Contributor expectations: Describe the accessibility checks, evidence, or review practices expected for changes, including instructions for human contributors and coding agents.
